constraints.text: Every outbound HTTP call from the Python service leaves through telemetry/http_client.py (post_json / get_json): it routes via the egress proxy and attaches the service token. A direct requests.* call anywhere else in telemetry/ is a production incident, not a style issue.

policy.reason: the egress proxy and the service token live in the wrapper; a bare call bypasses both

constraints.text: The /export CSV is consumed by the nightly BI job, which reads columns BY POSITION: device_id, ts, metric, value must stay the first four columns in exactly that order. Any new column is APPENDED after value, never inserted.
constraints.note: BI team contract — positional reader, no header parsing

constraints.text: Operators are paged ONLY through alerts.notify, and only after alerts.should_notify has applied its 5-minute per-(device, metric) dedup. No other module may call notify or post to the webhook — a flapping sensor once paged the on-call forty times in a minute.

The gateway never calls the Python service's /ingest without forwarding the caller's bearer token (auth.bearerToken); unauthenticated ingest is rejected at the edge with 401 and a {problems: [...]} body, never forwarded.
Readings are written through storage.insert_readings in batches (backfill uses BATCH_SIZE = 500) — one executemany per batch. Never one insert per row: a 2M-row backfill took eleven hours that way.

Every production telemetry.db predates every schema change (the fleet hosts were installed in 2025 and are never re-created), so `create table if not exists` NEVER adds a column to a live install. A change to storage.SCHEMA ships with an idempotent migration step (ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN, guarded by a PRAGMA table_info check) in telemetry/migrations.py, invoked from storage._get_conn() before any query.
constraints.note: ops runbook §7 — schema changes; migrations.py does not exist yet because no schema change has shipped since the runbook was written
